summary.one_line: Bob Johansson signs up for cryonic preservation, spends a day at a science-fiction convention, and is killed in a sudden traffic accident.
summary.paragraph: In 2016, human Bob Johansson visits CryoEterna and formally arranges to have his head cryonically preserved after death, seeing it as his only rational shot at continued existence. Flush from selling his software company, he spends the day at The Vortex science-fiction convention and later has lunch with former employees and friends, where he defends both cryonics and his humanist worldview. He also reconnects by phone with his mother and sister, showing the warmth of his family relationships beneath their teasing. That evening, while heading back out into the convention crowds, Bob is struck by a car and dies, abruptly turning his speculative investment in the future into an immediate necessity.
events: Bob visits CryoEterna and signs a contract for cryonic preservation after joking through the gruesome details with the sales rep Kevin.
He heads to The Vortex convention in Las Vegas and attends panels on interstellar exploration, extraterrestrial biology, and Von Neumann probes.
At lunch with Carl, Karen, and Alan, Bob talks about the breakup with Jenny, defends his cryonics decision, and enthusiastically explains self-replicating probes.
Back in his hotel room, Bob calls his mother and ends up talking with his family in their usual affectionate, sarcastic style.
When he goes back out toward the convention, a car swerves through the street chaos and hits him, and Bob dies as voices fade around him.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Bob spends the chapter trying to reclaim optimism and control after heartbreak, only to have his ordinary human life end without warning.
